scope: Repository-only preflight index of all 143 Grade 3 source excerpts, original task-sheet URL references, and current learner content metadata.
acceptancePolicy: Only individually verified Stage A/B/C element-level comparisons and authored/routed graded or teacher-led evidence can upgrade a lesson to READY_FOR_STAGE_D. This grade-wide preflight does not upgrade any lesson.

lessons.title: Make Sense of Data
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is to elicit students’ prior understandings of single-unit scale picture graphs and bar graphs in preparation for upcoming work with scaled bar graphs.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Interpret picture graphs and bar graphs to generate questions (orally and in writing) about the data.

lessons.title: Represent Data and Solve Problems
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve one- and two-step problems about data represented in bar graphs.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent data using bar graphs and picture graphs. Solve one- and two-step problems using addition and subtraction within 20.

lessons.title: Scaled Picture Graphs PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to read and answer questions about scaled picture graphs.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Interpret scaled picture graphs to generate questions (orally and in writing) about the data.

lessons.title: Create Scaled Picture Graphs
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to create a scaled picture graph to represent categorical data.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent data using scaled picture graphs.

lessons.title: Represent Data in Scaled Bar Graphs
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to create a scaled bar graph.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent data using scaled bar graphs.

lessons.title: Choose a Scale
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to consider the advantages and disadvantages of various bar graph scales.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Choose an appropriate scale for a bar graph that represents a given data set.

sourceActivities.name: Represent More Data in a Scaled Bar Graph

lessons.title: Answer Questions about Scaled Bar Graphs
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve one-step “how many more” and “how many fewer” problems based on data presented in a scaled bar graph.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve one-step “how many more” and “how many fewer” problems within 100, based on the data presented in scaled bar graphs.

sourceActivities.name: Questions about Favorite Time of the Year
Questions About Bugs in the Garden

lessons.title: More Questions about Scaled Bar Graphs
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many fewer” problems, based on data presented in a scaled bar graph.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many fewer” problems within 100, based on the data presented in scaled bar graphs.

sourceActivities.name: Use Bar Graphs to Solve Problems

lessons.title: Multiplication as Equal Groups
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use scaled picture graphs as an introduction to multiplication as equal groups.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Build an understanding of multiplication as equal groups. Represent a situation involving equal groups in a way that makes sense to students.

sourceActivities.name: From Scaled Graphs to Equal Groups

lessons.title: Drawings, Situations, and Diagrams, Oh My! PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to connect situations involving equal groups to tape diagrams.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Interpret a situation involving equal groups and represent it with a diagram. Make sense of tape diagrams that represent multiplication.

lessons.title: Multiplication Expressions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use multiplication expressions to represent equal groups.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Write multiplication expressions to represent situations involving equal groups and diagrams.

lessons.title: Represent and Solve Multiplication Problems
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to represent and solve multiplication problems.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent and solve multiplication problems.

lessons.title: Multiplication Equations
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to relate multiplication equations to situations and diagrams and write equations.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Relate equations to multiplication situations and diagrams. Write equations for multiplication situations and diagrams using a symbol for the unknown number.

lessons.title: Write and Solve Equations with Unknowns
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to relate equations to and write equations for multiplication situations and diagrams using a symbol for the unknown number.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Relate equations to multiplication situations and diagrams using a symbol for the unknown number. Write equations for multiplication situations and diagrams using a symbol for the unknown number.

sourceActivities.name: Write Equations with an Unknown Number

lessons.title: More Factors, More Problems
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve multiplication problems.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve multiplication problems.

lessons.title: Arrange Objects Into Arrays
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to describe arrays and arrange objects into arrays.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Build arrays with physical objects and describe them in terms of multiplication. Describe an array as an arrangement of objects into rows with an equal number of objects in each row and into columns with an equal number in each column.

lessons.title: Match and Draw Arrays
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to relate arrays to drawings of equal groups and describe arrays in terms of multiplication.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Relate arrays to drawings of equal groups and describe them in terms of multiplication.

lessons.title: Represent Arrays with Expressions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to represent multiplication situations with arrays and multiplication expressions.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent multiplication situations with arrays and multiplication expressions.

lessons.title: Solve Problems Involving Arrays
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to represent an array situation using an equation with a symbol for the unknown number and solve.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent an array situation with an equation with a symbol for the unknown number. Solve multiplication problems involving arrays.

lessons.title: The Commutative Property PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to describe the commutative property of multiplication using arrays.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Describe the commutative property of multiplication using arrays.

lessons.title: Game Night Seating Plan (optional)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use their understanding of equal groups to solve a design problem.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Make choices and assumptions. Represent data using scaled bar graphs to communicate results. Solve real-world problems involving equal groups.

lessons.title: What is Area? PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to recognize that different shapes cover different amounts of space.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Describe the relative size of plane figures in their own language.

lessons.title: How Do We Measure Area?
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use square tiles to build shapes and measure area.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Explore area by building shapes with unit squares. Use unit squares to measure area.

sourceActivities.name: Use Square Tiles to Measure Area

lessons.title: Tile Rectangles
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to measure area by counting square tiles and create rectangles with a given area.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Explain that rectangles that can be covered by the same number of unit squares without gaps or overlaps have the same area. Find the area of rectangles (within 24 square units) by counting unit squares.

lessons.title: Area of Rectangles
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to continue to count squares to create rectangles and to find the area of rectangles with larger numbers than in the previous lesson.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Describe and represent the area of a rectangle as the total number of unit squares arranged in equal groups of rows and columns. Find the area of rectangles (within 60 square units) by counting unit squares.

lessons.title: Represent Products as Areas PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to connect multiplication expressions to rectangular areas.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Relate multiplication to finding the area of rectangles.

lessons.title: Different Square Units (Part 1)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to learn that there are different units that can be used to measure area, specifically square centimeters and square inches .
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Describe square units based on different linear units of measurement. Use square inches and square centimeters to measure the area of a rectangle.

lessons.title: Different Square Units (Part 2)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to learn about square feet and square meters , and consider when these larger units can be helpful to measure area.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Use square feet and square meters to measure the area of a rectangle.

lessons.title: Area of Rectangles Without a Grid
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to determine the area of rectangles that are not fully gridded with squares.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Determine the area of rectangles not displayed on a grid.

lessons.title: Measure to Find the Area
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to measure side lengths of rectangles to find their area.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Find the area of rectangles by measuring and multiplying the side lengths.

lessons.title: Solve Area Problems
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve problems involving area.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area.

lessons.title: Area and the Multiplication Table (optional)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to explore connections between area and the multiplication table.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Explore connections between area and the multiplication table.

lessons.title: Area and Addition PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use gridded rectangles to learn that area is additive.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Find the area of figures composed of rectangles. Recognize that area is additive.

lessons.title: Find the Area of Figures
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to calculate the area of ungridded figures made of rectangles using multiplication and addition.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Calculate the area of ungridded figures made of rectangles using multiplication and addition.

sourceActivities.name: How Many Pavers Do We Need?

lessons.title: Find the Area of Figures with Missing Sides
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to calculate the area of ungridded figures made of rectangles, including figures with missing side lengths.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Calculate the area of ungridded figures composed of rectangles, including figures with missing side lengths.

lessons.title: New Room (optional)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use their experience with areas of figures composed of rectangles to solve problems.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve problems involving the area of ungridded figures composed of rectangles, including figures with missing side lengths.

lessons.title: Represent Numbers in Different Ways
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to represent numbers using base-ten blocks, base-ten diagrams, expanded form, numerals, and word form.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent numbers to 1,000 in different ways using place value understanding.

sourceActivities.name: Card Sort: Numbers in Their Different Forms
Numbers in Different Forms Round Table

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction Situations
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use addition and subtraction to solve problems within 1,000.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve addition and subtraction problems within 1,000 in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Add Your Way
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use strategies to add within 1,000.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Add within 1,000 in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Introduction to Addition Algorithms PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use their knowledge of base-ten diagrams to make sense of two written addition algorithms.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Add within 1,000. Relate base-ten diagrams to written algorithms for addition.

lessons.title: Another Addition Algorithm
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use an addition algorithm that records a single digit for the sum for each place value position and a 10 or 100 for a newly composed ten or hundred.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Relate written algorithms to each other using place value understanding.

lessons.title: Use Strategies and Algorithms to Add
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to record newly composed tens and hundreds with a single digit and to consider when they might use algorithms or other strategies to add.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Add within 1,000 using an algorithm or another strategy based on the numbers being added.

lessons.title: Subtract Your Way
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is to activate the strategies students have for subtracting numbers within 1,000.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Subtract within 1,000 in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Subtraction Algorithms (Part 1)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use their knowledge of base-ten diagrams to make sense of a written subtraction algorithm.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Relate base-ten diagrams to written algorithms for subtraction.

lessons.title: Subtraction Algorithms (Part 2)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to subtract within 1,000 using a subtraction algorithm that records numbers in expanded form.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Analyze and use a subtraction algorithm with the numbers written in expanded form.

lessons.title: Subtraction Algorithms (Part 3) PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use a subtraction algorithm that records a single digit for the difference between the numbers in each place value position and a condensed notation for a decomposed hundred or ten.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Relate subtraction algorithms to one another using place value understanding. Subtract numbers within 1,000 using another algorithm based on place value.

lessons.title: Analyze Subtraction Algorithms
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to consider subtraction algorithms in more detail, with a focus on decomposing as needed and on cases when it is necessary to decompose multiple units to subtract across zeros.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Analyze different steps in subtraction algorithms and reason about when certain steps might be more productive.

lessons.title: Subtract Strategically
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to consider when they might use algorithms or other strategies to subtract.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Subtract within 1,000 using algorithms or other strategies based on the numbers in the problem.

lessons.title: Multiples of 100 PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to reason about the position of numbers relative to their immediate multiples of 100, using number lines to do so.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Recognize that numbers are often approximated by their closest multiples of 10 or 100. Understand the meaning of the nearest multiple of 100.

lessons.title: Nearest Multiples of 10 and 100
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to reason about the position of numbers relative to their immediate multiples of 10 and 100, using number lines to do so.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Identify the closest multiples of 10 and 100 for numbers within 1,000. Understand that rounding is a formal way to say which number a given number is closer to, and that number is often a multiple of 10 or 100. Understand the meaning of “the closest multiple of 10.”

lessons.title: Round to the Nearest Ten and Hundred
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to round whole numbers within 1,000 to the nearest ten or hundred.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Round whole numbers within 1,000 to the nearest ten and hundred, using the convention of rounding up when the number is halfway between two multiples of 10 or 100.

sourceActivities.name: Can the Nearest Ten and Hundred be the Same?

lessons.title: Round and Round Again
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use their understanding of rounding to consider all the numbers that round to a given number.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Recognize and generalize patterns in the rounding of whole numbers within 1,000.

lessons.title: Does It Make Sense? PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use mental computation and estimation strategies such as rounding to decide if answers to two-step word problems make sense.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding. Solve two-step word problems using addition and subtraction in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Diagrams and Equations for Word Problems
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to relate diagrams and equations to two-step word problems.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Relate diagrams and equations to two-step word problems.

sourceActivities.name: Card Sort: Situations, Equations, and Diagrams
Makes Sense to Me: A Gallery Walk

lessons.title: Situations and Equations
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to represent and solve two-step word problems.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent and solve two-step word problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.

lessons.title: More Practice to Represent and Solve
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to continue to represent and solve two-step word problems, including problems in which not all necessary information is given up front.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent and solve two-step word problems.

lessons.title: Classroom Supplies (optional)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use their understanding of estimation, rounding, and addition within 1,000 to solve a problem about a class wish list.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Add and subtract within 1,000 to solve real-world problems. Round whole numbers to the nearest ten or hundred to solve problems.

lessons.title: How Many Groups?
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve “how many groups?” problems in a way that makes sense to them.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve “how many groups?” problems in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: How Many in Each Group?
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve “how many in each group?” problems in a way that makes sense to them.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve “how many in each group?” problems in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Division Situation Drawings
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to interpret descriptions or drawings of division situations and recognize whether they involve finding an unknown number of groups or finding an unknown number of objects in each group.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Interpret and relate drawings and descriptions of division situations. Understand that a division situation may involve finding an unknown number of groups or finding an unknown number of objects in each group.

lessons.title: Interpret Division Expressions PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to interpret division expressions and understand that the same division expression can be used to represent both types of division situations.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Interpret division expressions. Understand that the same division expression can be used to represent both types of division situations.

lessons.title: Write Division Expressions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to write division expressions to represent division situations and solve “how many groups?” and “how many in each group?” problems.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve “how many groups?” and “how many in each group?” problems. Write division expressions to represent division situations.

lessons.title: Division as an Unknown Factor
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to relate multiplication and division and recognize division as an unknown factor problem.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Explain the relationship between multiplication and division equations. Interpret division equations and multiplication equations with a missing factor.

lessons.title: Relate Multiplication and Division PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use the relationship between multiplication and division to write equations and solve problems.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent situations involving equal groups using multiplication and division equations with a symbol for the unknown quantity. Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve problems involving equal groups.

lessons.title: Relate Quotients to Familiar Products
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to practice identifying multiplication facts within 100 and to use products they know to determine unknown quotients.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Identify known single-digit multiplication facts and their related division facts.

sourceActivities.name: If I Know, Then I Know

lessons.title: Patterns in the Multiplication Table
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to identify and explain patterns in the multiplication table.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Identify arithmetic patterns in the multiplication table and use them to find unknown multiplication facts. Recognize that multiplication is commutative.

sourceActivities.name: If I Know, Then I Know: Multiplication

lessons.title: Explore Multiplication Strategies with Rectangles
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use area diagrams to explore multiplication strategies based on properties of operations.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Use area diagrams to explore strategies based on properties of multiplication.

lessons.title: Multiplication Strategies on Ungridded Rectangles
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to represent multiplication strategies on an ungridded rectangle.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply associative and distributive properties of multiplication to find products within 100. Recognize that multiplication is associative and can be distributed over addition.

sourceActivities.name: Card Sort: Different Expressions, Same Rectangle

lessons.title: Multiply Multiples of Ten
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations.

lessons.title: Solve Problems With Equal Groups
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve problems involving multiplication within 100, where one factor is a teen number, in a way that makes sense to them.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Multiply within 100, where one factor is a teen number, in a way that makes sense to them.

sourceActivities.name: Gallery Walk: Problems with Teen Numbers

lessons.title: Ways to Represent Multiplication of Teen Numbers PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to make sense of representations of the multiplication of teen numbers.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Make sense of representations of multiplication (base-ten blocks and area diagrams) where one factor is a teen number.

lessons.title: Equal Groups, Larger Numbers
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to multiply within 100, where one factor is a teen number.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Multiply within 100, where one factor is a teen number.

sourceActivities.name: Gallery Walk: Equal Groups, Larger Numbers

lessons.title: Multiply Numbers Larger than 20
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to multiply within 100, where one factor is greater than 20.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Multiply within 100, where one factor is greater than 20. Use properties based on place value and properties of operations to multiply.

lessons.title: Use the Four Operations to Solve Problems
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve two-step problems using all four operations.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent two-step word problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Solve two-step word problems using the four operations.

lessons.title: Larger Numbers in Equal Groups
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve problems involving division within 100, with quotients over 10, in a way that makes sense to them.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve problems involving division within 100, with quotients over 10, in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Ways to Divide Larger Numbers
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to recognize that the two interpretations of division still apply when dividing larger numbers and to use base-ten diagrams to interpret and represent division within 100.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Recognize that division of larger numbers can still mean finding the number of groups or finding the size of each group. Use base-ten blocks to represent division where the quotient is more than 10.

lessons.title: Strategies for Dividing
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to analyze representations and strategies for finding quotients with larger numbers and to divide within 100.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Analyze strategies for representing and reasoning about division. Divide within 100 using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

lessons.title: Solve Problems Using the Four Operations PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to represent and solve two-step word problems using the four operations.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent two-step word problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Solve two-step word problems using the four operations.

lessons.title: School Community Garden (optional)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is to use multiplication and division to model a real-world design problem.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent and solve “How many groups?” and “How many in each group?” problems in a real-world context. Solve two-step problems in a real-world context.

lessons.title: Name the Parts
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to be introduced to fractions as numbers we write to describe the parts of a whole that has been partitioned into equal parts.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Partition shapes into 2, 3, 4, 6, or 8 parts with equal area and name those parts as halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, and eighths. Recognize that equal-size parts in a shape can be named with numbers called fractions.

lessons.title: Name Parts as Fractions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to partition shapes into equal parts and express each equal-size part as a unit fraction.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole. Partition shapes into halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, and eighths.

lessons.title: Non-unit Fractions PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to understand non-unit fractions.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Understand a fraction $\frac{a}{b}$ as the quantity formed by $a$ parts of size $\frac{1}{b}$.

lessons.title: Build Fractions from Unit Fractions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to build non-unit fractions and whole numbers from unit fractions.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Build non-unit fractions and whole numbers from unit fractions.

lessons.title: To the Number Line
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to extend their understanding of whole numbers on the number line as they work with number lines partitioned into fractions.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Extend understanding of whole numbers on the number line to see fractions on a number line.

sourceActivities.name: Fold and Label the Number Line

lessons.title: Locate Unit Fractions on the Number Line
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to partition the interval from 0 to 1and locate unit fractions within that interval.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Partition the interval from 0 to 1 and locate unit fractions within that interval.

sourceActivities.name: Unit Fractions on the Number Line

lessons.title: Non-unit Fractions on the Number Line PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to locate non-unit fractions on the number line.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Locate non-unit fractions on the number line (including fractions greater than 1).

lessons.title: Fractions and Whole Numbers
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers and, given the location of a unit fraction on the number line, to locate whole numbers.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Locate whole numbers on the number line given the location of a unit fraction and express them as fractions. Recognize that whole numbers can be written as fractions.

lessons.title: All Kinds of Numbers on the Number Line
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use their knowledge of fractions on the number line to locate 1 when given a non-unit fraction.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Locate 1 on the number line given the location of a non-unit fraction.

lessons.title: Equivalent Fractions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to see that different fractions can be equivalent if they are the same size of the same whole.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Identify equivalent fractions. Understand two fractions as equivalent if they are the same size and the parts refer to the same whole.

lessons.title: Generate Equivalent Fractions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to generate equivalent fractions.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Use diagrams to explain or show fraction equivalence. Use diagrams to generate equivalent fractions.

lessons.title: Equivalent Fractions on a Number Line PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use the number line to determine whether fractions are equivalent.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Identify and generate equivalent fractions. Understand two fractions as equivalent if they are at the same point on a number line.

lessons.title: Whole Numbers and Fractions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers and write whole numbers as fractions.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Express whole numbers as fractions. Recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

lessons.title: How Do You Compare Fractions?
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to represent and compare fractions in a way that makes sense to them.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Represent and compare fractions in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Compare Fractions with the Same Denominator
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to compare two fractions with the same denominator.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Compare two fractions with the same denominator by reasoning about their size.

sourceActivities.name: Compare Fractions with the Same Denominator

lessons.title: Compare Fractions with the Same Numerator
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to compare two fractions with the same numerator.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Compare two fractions with the same numerator by reasoning about their size.

lessons.title: Compare Fractions PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator in and out of context and to justify their conclusions.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator. Record the results of comparison with the symbols >, =, or <.

lessons.title: Design With Fractions (optional)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to apply their understanding of fractions to create geometric designs.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply fraction understanding to create geometric designs.

lessons.title: Measure in Halves of an Inch
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to measure lengths that are fractions of an inch and relate these measurements to fractions on a number line.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Measure lengths using a ruler marked with halves of an inch.

lessons.title: Measure in Fourths of an Inch
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to measure length using a ruler marked with fourths of an inch.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Measure lengths using rulers marked with fourths of an inch.

lessons.title: Measure in Halves and Fourths of an Inch PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use what they know about fraction equivalence to measure with a ruler that is marked with halves and fourths of an inch.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Measure lengths using a ruler marked with both halves and fourths of an inch. Use equivalent fractions to describe length measurements.

lessons.title: Interpret Measurement Data on Line Plots
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to make sense of line plots that represent measurements to the nearest half or fourth of an inch.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Interpret line plots that display measurement data in fractions of an inch.

lessons.title: Represent Measurement Data on Line Plots
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to generate measurement data and represent them on a line plot.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Create a line plot where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters—to represent measurement data. Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using a ruler marked with halves and fourths of an inch.

lessons.title: Estimate and Measure Weight
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to learn to measure and estimate the weight of objects in grams or kilograms.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Measure and estimate weights of objects using standard units of grams (g) and kilograms (kg).

lessons.title: Introduction to Liquid Volume PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is to introduce students to the measurement of liquid volume.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Estimate and compare liquid volumes of containers using informal units and liters. Understand liquid volume as the amount of space that a liquid takes up.

lessons.title: Estimate and Measure Liquid Volume
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use liters to measure and estimate liquid volumes.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Measure and estimate liquid volumes of objects using standard units of liters (L).

lessons.title: Time to the Nearest Minute
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to tell and write time to the nearest minute.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Tell and write time to the nearest minute.

sourceActivities.name: Just a Clock on the Wall

lessons.title: Solve Problems Involving Time (Part 1) PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes in a way that makes sense to them.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Solve Problems Involving Time (Part 2)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes.

lessons.title: Ways to Represent Measurement Situations PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to make sense of situations involving measurements, interpret representations of the situations, and ask and answer questions about them.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Ask and answer questions about situations involving measurements. Interpret representations of situations involving measurements.

lessons.title: Problems with Missing Information
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to determine the information needed to solve problems involving weight.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Determine information that is needed to solve measurement problems. Solve one-step word problems involving weight.

lessons.title: What Makes Sense in the Problem?
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to consider quantities and questions that make sense in situations and solve problems accordingly.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Reason about quantities, questions, and solutions that make sense in measurement problems. Solve one-step word problems involving time and liquid volume.

lessons.title: Ways to Solve Problems and Show Solutions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve problems using the four operations as they imagine spending a day at the fair.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Analyze strategies for solving problems and for presenting solutions. Use the four operations to solve one-step word problems involving measurements.

sourceActivities.name: A Day at the Fair Gallery Walk

lessons.title: Design a Carnival Game (optional)
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to apply their understanding of length measurement, time measurement, and fluency with four operations to design a carnival game.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply knowledge of measurement and operations to design a game.

lessons.title: What Attributes Do You See?
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to sort shapes into categories based on their attributes.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Describe attributes of shapes. Sort shapes based on attributes in a way that makes sense to them.

lessons.title: Attributes of Triangles and Quadrilaterals
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use attributes of triangles and quadrilaterals to sort them into more specific categories.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Sort triangles and quadrilaterals into subcategories. Understand that shared attributes of shapes can define a larger category, such as triangle or quadrilateral.

lessons.title: Attributes that Define Shapes
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to describe geometric attributes of shapes.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Describe and identify shapes using their distinguishing attributes.

sourceActivities.name: Learn How to Play Mystery Quadrilateral

lessons.title: Attributes of Rectangles, Rhombuses, and Squares PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to consider the geometric attributes a quadrilateral must have to be a rhombus, rectangle, or square.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Identify attributes of rhombuses, rectangles, and squares.

lessons.title: Attributes of Other Quadrilaterals
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use their knowledge of geometric attributes to name quadrilaterals in different ways and to draw quadrilaterals that are not rhombuses, rectangles, or squares.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Draw examples of quadrilaterals that are not rhombuses, rectangles, or squares. Understand that shapes can be in more than one category.

lessons.title: Distance Around Shapes
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to understand perimeter and find the perimeter of shapes by counting to determine the side lengths.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Describe perimeter as the length of the boundary of a flat shape. Find the perimeter of two-dimensional shapes.

sourceActivities.name: What Does It Take to Build the Shapes?

lessons.title: Same Perimeter, Different Shapes
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to practice finding the perimeter of shapes and to understand that many different shapes can have the same perimeter.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Find the perimeter of two-dimensional shapes. Understand that many different shapes can have the same perimeter.

lessons.title: Find the Perimeter PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to find perimeters of shapes given all or some of the side lengths.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Find the perimeter of two-dimensional shapes given all or some of the side lengths.

lessons.title: Perimeter Problems
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to find unknown side lengths given the perimeter of a shape and solve problems involving perimeter.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Find unknown side lengths given the perimeter of a shape. Solve problems that involve perimeters of shapes.

lessons.title: Problem Solving With Perimeter and Area
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to solve problems that involve both perimeter and area of rectangles in order to reinforce the difference between perimeter and area.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve problems that involve perimeter and area of rectangles.

sourceActivities.name: Info Gap: A Garden and a Playground

lessons.title: Rectangles with the Same Perimeter PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to understand that rectangles with the same perimeter do not always have the same area.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Draw rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas.

lessons.title: Rectangles with the Same Area
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to understand that rectangles with the same area do not always have the same perimeter.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Draw rectangles with the same area and different perimeters.

lessons.title: Shapes and Play
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to consider how geometric attributes, perimeter, and area are used when designing a playground.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply geometric understanding to solve problems about parks.

lessons.title: Wax Prints PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to consider how geometric attributes, perimeter, and area are used to design and use wax print fabric.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply geometric understanding to solve problems about wax prints.

lessons.title: Design Your Own Robot
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to draw rectangles with specified perimeters to create a robot.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply geometric understanding to solve problems about robots.

lessons.title: Estimation Explorations with Fractions
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to practice reasoning about fraction representations through estimation.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Estimate fractions represented in diagrams and on number lines.

lessons.title: Create Your Own Number Line
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to create their own number line to represent and compare fractions.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <. Represent fractions on a number line.

lessons.title: Fractions Round Table PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to consider statements about fractions that will help them solidify their understanding of fractions as numbers.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Generalize key ideas about fractions, such as what fractions mean, whole numbers as fractions, and fraction comparisons.

lessons.title: Tiny House: Design and Solve PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to design and solve problems about a tiny house.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply understanding of area and perimeter to solve problems about design.

lessons.title: Tiny House: Cost
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to apply what they’ve learned about operations to calculate the cost to finish a space in a tiny house.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Solve problems about the cost of finishing a room in a tiny house.

lessons.title: Survey the Class, Survey the School
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use a survey to collect a data set with several categories.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Collect categorical data to create a data set with several categories.

lessons.title: Graph and Answer
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to draw a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Draw a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

lessons.title: Multiplication Center Day
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to evaluate their fluency with multiplication within 100.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Practice multiplication within 100. Reflect on multiplication fluency.

lessons.title: Multiplication Game Day
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to practice multiplying within 100.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Practice finding products within 100 by playing multiplication games.

sourceActivities.name: Introduce Rectangle Rumble and How Close?

lessons.title: Multiplication and Division PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to use a variety of representations to illustrate the relationship between multiplication and division to develop fluency with division within 100.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Interpret representations of the relationship between multiplication and division. Represent the relationship between multiplication and division.

lessons.title: Division Game Day
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to develop fluency with dividing within 100.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Practice dividing whole numbers within 100.

lessons.title: Notice and Wonder
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to apply their understanding of equal groups to create a Notice and Wonder activity.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply understanding of equal groups to create a Notice and Wonder activity.

lessons.title: How Many Do You See? PLC Activity
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to apply their understanding of equal groups and multiplication to create a How Many Do You See activity.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply understanding of equal groups and multiplication to create a How Many Do You See activity.

sourceActivities.name: Design Your How Many Do You See
Facilitate Your How Many Do You See

lessons.title: Estimation Exploration
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to apply their understanding of measurement of fractional lengths to create an Estimation Exploration activity.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply understanding of measuring objects to the nearest half and fourth of an inch to create an Estimation Exploration activity.

lessons.title: Number Talk
lessons.originalTeacherPurposeExcerpt: The purpose of this lesson is for students to apply their understanding of addition and subtraction to create a Number Talk activity.
lessons.originalTeacherLearningGoalsExcerpt: Apply understanding of addition and subtraction within 1,000 to create a Number Talk activity.
